 Oral Order
Learned counsel for the petitioner is absent.
No representation.

Learned counsel for respondent
No.2 is present.

2. A letter is received from the Assistant Registrar, Supreme Court of India, transmitting the order
dated 23.08.2024 along with the settlement agreement dated 01.08.2024 passed therein.

3. The settlement agreement arrived at between the parties, reads as under:
"This settlement Agreement is being executed between Petitioner/Ms. Stuti
Khandelwal, D/o Shri Sudhir Khandelwal, R/o 433- Miracles Beauty Parlor,
Howbhag Station Road, Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh (hereinafter referred to as
Petitioner/wife) And Nc: 2024:Khc:50766 Mr. Anurag Grover S/o Shri Rajesh
Grover, R/o Mig-7, Mp Housing Board Colony, Polipather, Narmada Road,
Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh (hereinafter referred to as Respondent/husband)
1.

The marriage between the Petitioner and Respondent was solemnized as per Hindu
rites and customs on 15th February, 2020 at Gorakhpur Gurudwara, Jabalpur,
Madhya Pradesh.

The marriage was registered at Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh on 2nd
March 2020.

Both the parties resided together as husband and wife till 5th May,
2020.

That thereafter, due to some differences between the parties, they started
living separately.
Since then, onwards, both parties are residing separately.

There is
no issue from this wedlock.

2. The Petitioner/wife filed petition under section 10 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955
bearing Rcs Hm no. 455 of 2020 and an application under section 24 of the Hindu
Marriage Act, 1955 before the 1st Additional Principal Judge, Family Court, Jabalpur.
Sri Anurag Grover vs The State Of Karnataka on 9 December, 2024

2

Thereafter the Respondent/husband on 24th November, 2021 filed the Divorce
Petition under Section 13(1) (ia) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 bearing M.C. No.
6095 of 2021 titled Anurag Grover Vs. Stuti Khandelwal before 2nd Additional
Principal Judge, Family Court at Bengaluru, Karnataka.

The Transfer Petition (C) No. 2007 of 2023 was filed by the Petitioner/wife before
this Hon'ble Court seeking transfer of petition M.C. 6095 of 2021 titled Anurag
Grover Vs. Stuti Khandelwal filed by the Husband/Respondent pending before the
2nd Additional Principal Judge, Family Court at Bengaluru, Karnataka to the family
Court, Jabalpur (M.P).

4. That, vide Order dated 21.03.2024 passed by Hon'ble Mr. Justice Pamidighantam
Sri Narasimha and Hon'ble Mr. Justice Arvind Kumar, these matters have been
referred to the Supreme Court Mediation Centre for exploring settlement.

Comprehensive mediation sessions were held with the parties separately and jointly
on 09.04.2024, 26.04.2024 and 27.04.2024 (Virtual and Physical Both).

But, the
mediation via supreme court mediation center has failed, however both the parties
have mutually and amicably settled their dispute outside the court.
5. Both the parties
hereto

confirm and declare that they have voluntarily and of their own free-will,
decided to sever their ties as husband and wife, and have arrived at the following Settlement and,
have agreed to part ways amicably and to fully and finally settle the disputes and differences Nc:
2024:Khc:50766 and withdraw all proceedings filed against each other, as mentioned herein after.

That the following cases are pending between the parties, apart from the above Transfer Petitions: -
(i) F.I.R. No.77 of 2020 dated 08.05.2020 under Sections 34, 498A, 323, 504 of Ipc
registered by the Petitioner/Wife at Police Station Hsr, Layout, Bengaluru.

(ii) Judicial separation Petition filed under section 10 and an application under
section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 bearing Rcs Hm No. 455 of 2020, filed
by the Petitioner/wife pending before the 1st Additional Principal Judge, Family
Court, Jabalpur.

(iii) Divorce Petition filed under Section 13(1) (ia) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 bearing M.C.
No.6095 of 2021, filed by the Respondent/Husband, titled Anurag Grover Vs. Stuti Khandelwal
pending before 2nd Additional Principal Judge, Family Court at Bengaluru, Karnataka.

(iv) Criminal Proceeding initiated against the Respondent/ Husband arising out of the aforesaid
Fir, bearing No. Cc 14650 of 2020 Nc: 2024:Khc:50766 pending before 39th Acmm at
Bengaluru, Karnataka.

Quashing Petition filed by the Respondent/Husband of the aforesaid Fir under Section 482 of
Cr.P.C. bearing No. Crl.P.No.8159 of 2022 pending before the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka.
6.

That, except the above-mentioned cases in Para No.5 and above Transfer Petition, no other case is
pending between the parties.

7. The Respondent/husband shall pay the amount of Rupees 15,00,000/- (Rupees Fifteen Lakhs
Only) as full and final settlement to the Petitioner/wife through Demand Draft/Bankers Cheque and
shall also return all the original documents including 10th marksheet, 12th marksheet, B.com
bachelor degree/marksheets along with other documents on the day of passing of the order
dissolving the marriage and quashing of criminal proceeding initiated against the
respondent/husband arising out of Fir No.77 of 2020 dated 08/05/2020, bearing No. Cc 14650 of
2020 pending before the 39th Acmm at Bengaluru, Karnataka and any other civil/criminal
litigations arising out of the marriage.

The above amount of Rupees 15,00,000/ (Rupees Fifteen
Lakhs Only) has been paid to Stuti Khandelwal, Petitioner/wife Nc: 2024:Khc:50766 vide Bankers
Cheque No.317135 dated 29/07/2024 of State Bank of India, Nayagaon Branch, Jabalpur and also
returned the documents as mentioned above.
8. That, it is agreed between both the Parties
Respondent/husband and Petitioner/wife

shall jointly
move an application for directions before the Hon'ble Supreme Court to exercise its inherent power
under Article 142 of the Constitution of India for relief of divorce, Judicial Separation Petition and
dispose/quash all the other pending civil/criminal proceedings/disputes in terms of the present
settlement agreement between the parties.

9. The belongings including clothes, footwears, handbags, perfumes, cosmetics, bed sheets,
suitcases, wallets and fashion jewellery shall be handed over to the petitioner/wife on the day of
signing of this settlement agreement.

On signing of this settlement agreement by the
petitioner/wife, the belonging as mentioned above has been handed over to the petitioner/wife.

10. That, both the parties have agreed to co- operate with each other to bring an amicable end to the
disputes between the Parties, and not to initiate any further legal proceedings against each other or
their family members.

It is agreed between the Parties that they shall have no right title or interest over the movable or
immovable properties of each other.

12. It is agreed between the parties that the parties or their parents/relatives shall be free to live
their life independently without interference of any kind from each other or their family members.

13. It is agreed between the parties that they shall be left with no matrimonial rights towards each
other and shall not litigate against each other and their respective family members qua the present
marriage in future.
